issues.legal_issue: A Hindu undivided family previously assessed as undivided continues to be treated as such for tax purposes when a partition is claimed but no order apportioning tax liability on the basis of that partition has been made.
material_facts: The family had previously been assessed as a Hindu undivided family.
The appellant claimed that the family had partitioned and that tea estates had fallen to his share.
No order apportioning tax liability on the basis of the claimed partition had been made.
The appellant challenged assessments made in respect of agricultural income from the tea estates.
issues.conclusion: The family was to be treated as continuing to be a Hindu undivided family for the purposes of the Act because no order apportioning liability on the basis of the alleged partition had been passed.
issues.legal_principle: Rule 23 of the Assam Agricultural Income-tax Rules, 1939 provides that a Hindu family hitherto assessed as undivided or joint is deemed to continue in that status for the purposes of the Act unless an order apportioning tax liability on the basis of partition is made. The Court held that the language of the rule is clear and applies even where the assessment in question is not merely a recovery of tax under an earlier assessment.

rule.if: tax_assessment_challenge and prior_joint_assessment and partition_claimed and not apportionment_order_passed

predicates.tax_assessment_challenge: The proceeding challenges an assessment of tax on income attributed to a family previously assessed as undivided or joint.
predicates.prior_joint_assessment: The taxing authority had previously assessed the family as undivided or joint.
predicates.partition_claimed: A member of the family claimed that the family had partitioned.
predicates.apportionment_order_passed: The taxing authority made an order apportioning tax liability on the basis of the claimed partition.
predicates.family_treated_as_joint_for_tax_purposes: The family is treated as continuing to be undivided or joint for tax purposes.

issues.definition: When an assessment challenge concerns a family previously assessed as joint, and a partition is claimed but no apportionment order has been made, the family is treated as joint for tax purposes.

issues.legal_issue: A rule made under a general power to carry out the purposes of a tax statute is valid when it fills in implementation details, including identifying the person to be assessed, rather than creating the tax liability itself.
material_facts: The Act's charging section imposed tax on agricultural income of specified persons, including Hindu undivided families.
The State Government had authority to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, and the rules had been previously published.
The challenged rule provided how a family previously assessed as undivided or joint was to be treated after a claimed partition unless an apportionment order was made.
The appellant challenged the State Government's competence to make the rule.
issues.conclusion: The State Government was competent to make the rule, which was within its rule-making power and was valid.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3 of the Assam Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1939 created the tax liability, while section 50(1) empowered the State Government to make rules to carry out the Act's purposes; section 50(2)(j) specifically addressed the manner in which tax was payable following certain partitions. The rule dealt with the detail of who should be assessed and did not create the tax liability. The Court held that it is permissible for a legislature to leave executive authorities to determine details in the working of taxation laws, relying on Pt. Banarsi Das v. State of Madhya Pradesh, which approved Powell v. Apollo Candle Company Limited and Syed Mohamed & Co. v. State of Madras. The Court also noted the analogous treatment of Hindu undivided families under section 171 of the Income-tax Act, 1961.

rule.if: delegated_tax_rule_validity_challenge and law_authorizes_implementation_rules and prior_publication and law_imposes_tax_liability and rule_identifies_assessable_person and rule_fills_implementation_detail and rule_within_enabling_power

predicates.delegated_tax_rule_validity_challenge: The proceeding challenges the validity of a rule made by an executive authority under a tax statute.
predicates.law_authorizes_implementation_rules: The legislature authorized the executive authority to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the tax law.
predicates.prior_publication: The rule was published in advance as required before it was made.
predicates.law_imposes_tax_liability: The legislature itself imposed the underlying tax liability.
predicates.rule_identifies_assessable_person: The rule determines which person is to be assessed in respect of the taxable income.
predicates.rule_fills_implementation_detail: The rule deals with a detail needed to implement the tax law rather than imposing the underlying tax liability.
predicates.rule_within_enabling_power: The subject addressed by the rule falls within the authority the legislature delegated to the executive authority.
predicates.delegated_tax_rule_is_valid: The delegated tax rule is valid.

issues.definition: A challenged tax rule is valid when the legislature authorizes implementation rules, the required prior publication occurs, the law imposes the tax liability, and the rule identifies the person to be assessed as an implementation detail within the delegated authority.
